definition: The programmatic evaluation and dispatch of input prompts to optimal downstream models based on intent, complexity, and cost criteria.
details: Prompt routing prevents over-provisioning inference by triaging user requests using small classification heads or semantic embeddings, reserving large frontier models for complex multi-step reasoning while routing simpler tasks to smaller edge models.

explainer.lead: Prompt routing evaluates and dispatches input prompts to the most suitable downstream model based on intent, complexity and cost. It matters because it avoids over-provisioning inference, reserving large models for hard tasks.

tiers.eli5: It is like a hospital triage nurse who sends simple cases to a nurse and complex ones to a specialist, so no one wastes a specialist's time.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers triage requests with small classification heads or semantic embeddings, sending complex multi-step reasoning to frontier models and simpler tasks to smaller edge models. A pitfall is misrouting a hard request to a model too small to handle it.
tiers.paperLevel: Routing is programmatic evaluation and dispatch of prompts to optimal downstream models based on intent, complexity and cost criteria, using small classification heads or semantic embeddings. Routing decisions bound which model handles a given request.

explainer.example: A semantic embedding classifies a simple lookup question and routes it to a small edge model, while a multi-step reasoning request goes to a frontier model.

citation.title: FrugalGPT: How to Use Large Language Models While Reducing Cost and Improving Performance
